scope: 28 requested stranded members plus 3 additionally listed source members. Three confirmed outer archive convictions retained without re-judgment.
method: atomscan and cleave facts for all 34 paths; direct source control/data-flow review; both native entry paths and scalar XOR decoders disassembled with rizin; both native script bodies independently decrypted; all traversal ZIP local/central names and bodies verified; WAR members read; ZIP bomb raw-DEFLATE decoding bounded to 1 MiB. No payload executed.
changes: Add a notable, correctly placed bulk Notes-property enumeration capability.
Add a suspicious co-occurrence of bulk Notes-property reads and a password-phishing signal; this does not prove unauthorized Notes reads or a source-to-send flow.
Add a suspicious sparse-string helper-state-XOR and osascript composite, recognizing both x86-64 and ARM64 transforms via existing atoms.
criticality_review: The new Notes co-occurrence composite is suspicious, not hostile: the generic password-prompt signal and bulk property query do not bind a phished value to Notes access or establish unauthorized transfer. Existing hostile convictions are unchanged.
consumer_review: The collection ancestor consumers require additional webhook/OOB or family context and mostly disjoint file types. Obfuscation ancestor consumers likewise require separate delivery/JavaScript context. No existing directory selectors target property enumeration. All before/after member and archive findings are compared below.

classifier_disagreement.explanation: Classifier calibration misses remain despite supported hostile static detections. Exact probabilities are retained for transparency and are not treated as verdicts. Model v18.18 warns that the extractor expects feature version 19. Rules were not weakened or duplicated to manipulate classifier scores.

scan_limitations: The initial before invocation mistakenly passed none as a second path after optional --follow; the target paths still emitted valid reports. All after scans use --follow=none. Initial-invocation variations and diagnostics are retained separately; initial and after full scans logged pre-existing rule hard timeouts. members.marker_note: Installer stealer: phishes, steals, persists; add Notes/XOR traits
members.evidence: Universal x86-64/ARM64 Mach-O launches an LCG-XOR-decrypted osascript command via system(). Both 37077-byte payloads decrypt identically: seed 0x11667, uint32(state*0x3785) % 35999, ciphertext offsets 0x4c90 and 0x14de0. x86-64 main calls system at 0x10000065c; ARM64 at 0x1000006b8. The reachable main handler validates ~/.pwd using dscl, otherwise loops a masked Installation password dialog. It saves and stages the password; copies Chromium, Firefox and Safari secrets, wallet stores, Keychain data, Notes, and selected Desktop/Documents files; archives staging with ditto; POSTs the archive using curl; removes staging; replaces Ledger Live from a downloaded ZIP; and installs a KeepAlive/RunAtLoad system LaunchDaemon using the captured password. The daemon UserName selects the current user, so installation privilege does not prove root execution. Notes automation is a fallback if direct NoteStore collection fails. The configured external endpoint and collected secrets establish malicious purpose independently of the enclosing package verdict.

members.marker_note: Laudanum JSP: request-command payload with broken IP-check syntax
members.evidence: Standalone Laudanum JSP source: request cmd is passed to Runtime.exec and process output is printed. The IP guard compares Java String references with != rather than value equality, and response.sendError(...) lacks a semicolon. The source is therefore not compilable as supplied; the embedded WAR JSP is a distinct functional unguarded payload. No successful deployment is asserted.
members.context: Executable/injectable attack payload or exploit specimen; legitimate testing distribution is acknowledged. No authorization, deployed-server history or victim execution evidence is supplied. The verdict concerns this payload role, not an inference that every use of its parent project is unauthorized.
